glosses.notes: The area outside a city, usually quieter and more open than the busy center.

examples.sentence: 周末一家人开车去郊外看花，回来以后孩子还一直说那边的路宽、车少，空气也比城里好。
新学校搬到郊外以后，老师每天都得更早出门，不然路上一慢下来，就很容易赶不上第一节课。
他们原来想在城里找地方住，后来还是搬到郊外，因为那边安静一些，孩子晚上也更容易睡好。

example_translations.translation: One weekend the whole family drove out to the suburbs to look at flowers, and even after coming back the child kept saying that the roads there were wider, there were fewer cars, and the air was better than in the city.
After the new school moved to the suburbs, the teacher had to leave even earlier every day, because if traffic slowed down on the road, it became easy to miss the first class.
They had originally wanted to find a place to live in the city, but later they still moved to the suburbs, because it was quieter there and the child could sleep better at night.

glosses.notes: A corner or out-of-the-way part of a room, street, building, or other place.

examples.sentence: 孩子把小球放在角落以后，一回头就忘了，后来还是老师看见了才帮他拿回来。
母亲在房间里面的角落找到那个旧盒子时，才想起里面还放着多年以前写过的信。
店里那个小角落平时人不多，一下雨以后，反而总有人坐在那里看外面的路和车。

example_translations.translation: After the child put the small ball in the corner, he forgot it as soon as he turned around, and later it was still the teacher who noticed it and helped bring it back.
When Mother found that old box in the corner of the room, she remembered that it still held letters written many years earlier.
That little corner of the shop usually does not have many people, but once it rains, people instead often sit there watching the road and the cars outside.

glosses.notes: A footprint or shoeprint left on the ground, snow, sand, mud, or another surface.

examples.sentence: 雪地里那一串脚印一直通到小门边上，父亲顺着它慢慢走过去，才发现猫早就已经进门了。
下过雨以后，门口地上留下了很多脚印，母亲刚拖完一遍，转身一看，又有人从外面走进来了。
孩子沿着脚印去找那只小狗，结果走到树后面才发现，它其实一直坐在车边没有动。

example_translations.translation: That trail of footprints in the snow went all the way to the small gate, and only after Father followed it over slowly did he discover that the cat had already gone in through the door.
After the rain, many footprints were left on the ground by the door. Mother had just mopped it once, and when she turned around, someone else was already walking in from outside.
The child followed the footprints to look for that little dog, but when he got behind the tree he found that it had actually been sitting still by the car the whole time.

glosses.notes: A formal way to say that something is relatively or comparatively so.

examples.sentence: 和原来的安排比起来，这个新办法较为简单，大家一看就知道先做哪一步，不会像以前那样乱。
老师说这篇文章前半段较为好懂，所以大家先从那里开始看，再一点一点往后面走会更容易。
这家小店地方不大，东西摆得较为整齐，所以第一次进来的人也不太会一下找不到要买的东西。

example_translations.translation: Compared with the original arrangement, this new method is relatively simple, and everyone can tell at a glance which step to do first instead of getting confused the way they used to.
The teacher said that the first half of this article is relatively easy to understand, so if everyone starts there and then moves gradually toward the later part, it will be easier.
This little shop is not big, and the goods are arranged comparatively neatly, so even people coming in for the first time are not too likely to fail to find what they came to buy.

glosses.notes: Can mean a lesson learned from a bad experience, or the act of teaching someone not to repeat a mistake.

examples.sentence: 这次把钥匙忘在车里，给了他一个不小的教训，所以后来不管多急，下车以前他都会先摸一遍身上。
父亲没有当场大声骂他，只是想借这件事教训他一次，让他以后做事以前先想清楚后果。
老人常说，年轻时吃过的教训如果一直记得住，到后面很多看起来大的问题反而就不会再犯。

example_translations.translation: This time, forgetting his keys in the car taught him quite a lesson, so later on, no matter how rushed he was, before getting out he would always first pat himself down once.
Father did not shout at him loudly on the spot. He simply wanted to use this matter to teach him a lesson, so that in the future he would think clearly about the consequences before doing things.
The old man often says that if the lessons you suffered when young are remembered clearly, then later on many problems that look big will actually not be repeated.

glosses.notes: Used for plants bearing fruit, or more broadly for something gradually producing a visible result.

examples.sentence: 院子里那棵老树今年结得特别多，母亲每天早上出去看一眼，回来都还要笑着和大家再说一遍。
这种树开花以后还要再等一些天才会开始结，所以老人每天看它的时候都比别人更有耐心。
那片地去年不太好，今年总算开始结了，父亲看见以后连回家路上都一直在笑。

example_translations.translation: The old tree in the yard bore an especially large amount of fruit this year. Every morning Mother went out to look at it once, and when she came back she would still smile and tell everyone again.
After this kind of tree flowers, you still have to wait some days before it starts to bear fruit, so the old man is more patient than other people when he looks at it each day.
That patch of land did not do very well last year, but this year it finally started bearing fruit, and after seeing that, Father kept smiling even on the way home.

glosses.notes: Used for a plant or tree producing fruit after flowering.

examples.sentence: 院子里那棵老树今年终于结果了，所以母亲每天早上出去看一眼，回来都还要笑着跟大家再说一遍。
这种树开花以后还要再等一些天才会结果，所以老人每天看它的时候都比别人更有耐心。
这棵树去年一直没有结果，今年天气一暖起来，父亲就天天出去看它。

example_translations.translation: The old tree in the yard finally bore fruit this year, so Mother went out to look at it every morning and came back smiling to tell everyone about it again.
After this kind of tree flowers, you still have to wait a few more days before it sets fruit, so the old man is more patient than other people when he checks it each day.
This tree did not bear fruit at all last year. As soon as the weather turned warm this year, Father started going out to check on it every day.

glosses.notes: Used when things happen or appear one after another without much break in between.

examples.sentence: 这几天接连下雨，门口那条小路一直干不了，所以大家进来的时候都得先把鞋底擦一擦。
她刚坐下就接连收到两个电话，一个是学校打来的，另一个是家里人问她什么时候回来。
店里接连关了几天门以后，旁边卖菜的人还以为老板生病了，后来才知道他只是回老家了。

example_translations.translation: It has rained day after day these past few days, so the little path by the door has never fully dried, and everyone has to wipe their shoe bottoms first when coming in.
She had only just sat down when she received two phone calls one after another, one from the school and the other from family members asking when she would be back.

After the shop had stayed closed for several days in a row, the people selling vegetables next to it thought the owner had fallen ill, and only later learned that he had simply gone back to his hometown.

glosses.notes: Describes something as solid and strong, or a person's body as strong and well-built.

examples.sentence: 这张旧桌子看着普通，其实特别结实，孩子在上面放书、写字，用了几年也一直没有坏。
孩子今年明显比去年更结实了，连以前一跑就累的那段路，现在也能跟着大家一起走完。
这双鞋虽然不算新，做得却很结实，所以父亲下雨天出门的时候还是最爱穿它。

example_translations.translation: This old desk looks ordinary, but it is actually very sturdy. The child puts books on it and writes on it, and even after years of use it still has not broken.
This year the child is clearly stronger and sturdier than last year. Even the stretch of road that used to make him tired after running is now something he can finish with everyone else.
Although this pair of shoes is not new, it is made very sturdily, so when Father goes out on rainy days, it is still the pair he likes wearing most.

glosses.notes: The street, street corner, or public street scene, especially in everyday urban life.

examples.sentence: 周末晚上街头还是很多人，孩子一边走一边看路边那些灯，回家以后还一直问什么时候再去。
大雨停了以后，街头很快又有卖吃的人出来了，大家站在边上看一会儿，就知道这地方又活了。
父亲在街头听见那首老歌以后，一下就想到年轻的时候，所以回家路上一直没有怎么说话。

example_translations.translation: There are still many people out on the streets on weekend nights. The child kept looking at the lights by the roadside while walking, and even after getting home he kept asking when they could go again.
After the heavy rain stopped, people selling food soon came back out onto the street, and after watching for a moment, everyone could tell that the place had come alive again.
After Father heard that old song on the street, he immediately thought of his younger days, so on the way home he barely spoke at all.

glosses.notes: Describes a person, work, or achievement as especially outstanding and far above the ordinary level.

examples.sentence: 老师说，真正杰出的人不只是自己做得好，还能让身边原来没有信心的人也慢慢敢往前走。
那位杰出的医生每次看完病都还会多问一句家里的情况，所以很多老人一直特别信任他。
村里人都知道他年轻时是个很杰出的工人，因为最难做的活一到他手里，总会变得顺很多。

example_translations.translation: The teacher says that truly outstanding people do not just do their own work well; they can also slowly help people around them who once lacked confidence dare to keep moving forward.
That outstanding doctor always asks one extra question about the family's situation after finishing an appointment, so many older people have continued to trust him deeply.
People in the village all know that when he was young he was an outstanding worker, because whenever the hardest tasks reached his hands, they always became much smoother.

glosses.notes: To use less power or fuel, or to make something work in a more energy-saving way.

examples.sentence: 家里换了新灯以后明显更节能，所以母亲每次看见电表的时候，心里都比前几年轻松一些。
老师提醒大家少开一会儿空调，不是为了小气，而是想让整栋楼一起慢慢养成节能的习惯。
这辆车看着不大，开起来比原来那辆更节能，所以父亲现在出远门时还是更爱开它。

example_translations.translation: After the house switched to new lights, it was clearly more energy-saving, so each time Mother looked at the electric meter, she felt a little more at ease than in past years.
The teacher reminded everyone to run the air conditioner a little less, not out of stinginess, but because she wanted the whole building to slowly build an energy-saving habit together.
This car does not look big, but it uses less energy than the previous one when driven, so Father still prefers to drive it now when going far from home.

glosses.notes: The ending of a story, speech, book, film, or other piece, or the act of bringing it to an end.

examples.sentence: 这本书的结尾来得很慢，孩子看完以后还是坐在那里想了很久，连水凉了都没有发现。
老师让我们先写中间，再想结尾，因为如果前面没有想清楚，到最后那几句也很难写好。
电影快要结尾的时候，原来一直在说话的人也慢慢安静下来，因为大家都想看最后怎么走。

example_translations.translation: The ending of this book came very slowly, but after finishing it the child still sat there thinking for a long time and did not even notice that the water had gone cold.
The teacher told us to write the middle first and then think about the ending, because if the earlier part has not been thought through clearly, the final lines are also hard to write well.
When the film was nearing its end, even the people who had been talking all along gradually quieted down, because everyone wanted to see how it would finally turn out.

glosses.notes: Used to mark a point up to which numbers, time, or facts are being counted or stated.

examples.sentence: 截至今天晚上，学校收到的报名表已经比去年多了很多，所以老师们连晚饭以后都还在看。

examples.meaning_en: up to a point in time
examples.sentence: 截至上周，这条路修到哪一段、还差多少，墙上的那张表都写得很清楚。
新闻里说，截至昨天晚上，大家最关心的几个问题已经有人出来回答了，所以家里人也放心一些。

example_translations.translation: As of tonight, the school has already received far more registration forms than it did last year, so the teachers are still reviewing them even after dinner.
Up to last week, how far this road had been repaired and how much was still left were both written clearly on the chart on the wall.
The news said that as of last night, several of the questions people cared about most had already been answered, so the family felt somewhat more at ease.

glosses.notes: Used when something stops, closes, or reaches its deadline.

examples.sentence: 这次报名明天中午就截止了，还有很多人没有交，所以老师今天一天都在提醒。
活动原来说好晚上八点截止，后来人一直很多，负责人只好多开一会儿门。
因为雨太大，比赛只好提前截止，很多原来还想再往前跑的人站在边上看了很久。

example_translations.translation: Registration for this round closes at noon tomorrow, and many people still have not turned theirs in, so the teacher has been reminding them all day.
The event was originally supposed to end at eight in the evening, but later there were still so many people that the person in charge had to keep the door open a little longer.
Because the rain was too heavy, the race had to be cut short ahead of time, and many people who had wanted to keep going stood on the side watching for a long time.

glosses.notes: The rhythm or pace of music, speech, work, life, or movement.

examples.sentence: 这首歌的节奏一快起来，原来坐着不动的人也会跟着轻轻点头，连孩子都知道哪里要拍手。
这几天工作节奏突然快了很多，所以大家中午吃饭的时候都比平常安静，只想先坐一会儿。
老师提醒我们别被别人说话的节奏带乱，先把自己心里那条线看清楚，再决定下一步怎么走。

example_translations.translation: When the rhythm of this song speeds up, even the people who had been sitting still start nodding lightly along with it, and even the children know where to clap.
The work pace has suddenly become much faster these past few days, so when everyone eats lunch, they are quieter than usual and only want to sit for a while first.
The teacher reminded us not to let the rhythm of other people's speech throw us off. We should first see clearly the line in our own minds and then decide how to take the next step.

glosses.notes: Can mean to untie, loosen, remove, or solve something that is tied up or difficult.

examples.sentence: 孩子回到家以后，先坐在门边慢慢把手上的带子解开，然后才想起来自己还没有把书放回房间。
那个结太紧，她解了半天还是没有开，只好把东西先放下，等父亲回来以后再一起看。
老师让大家先自己解这道题，真的走不下去的时候，再把卡住的地方一点一点问出来。

example_translations.translation: After the child got home, he first sat by the door and slowly untied the strap on his hand, and only then remembered that he still had not put his book back in the room.
That knot was too tight. She spent a long time trying to undo it and still could not open it, so she had to set the thing down first and wait for Father to come back and look at it together.
The teacher told everyone to solve the problem on their own first, and only when they really could not keep going should they ask bit by bit about the place where they got stuck.

glosses.notes: To answer a question or explain it clearly enough that another person understands.

examples.sentence: 老师下课以后还站在门口解答大家的问题，所以最后一个离开的人走的时候，天都已经比刚才暗多了。
节目里那位医生没有急着下结论，而是先一步一步解答家长最想问的几个问题，让大家别乱想。
这本书后面专门留了几页来解答常见问题，所以第一次看的人也不太会走到一半就停下。

example_translations.translation: After class, the teacher still stood by the door answering everyone's questions, so by the time the last person left, the sky was already much darker than before.
The doctor on the program did not rush to a conclusion, but first answered step by step the several questions parents most wanted to ask, so that everyone would stop imagining the worst.
Several pages are specially left at the back of this book to answer common questions, so even people reading it for the first time are not too likely to stop halfway through.

glosses.notes: To interpret, read out, or explain the meaning of a text, event, sign, statement, or result.

examples.sentence: 老师没有马上给出标准答案，而是先带着大家一点一点解读那几句话，看看里面到底想说什么。
新闻里请来的那位专家很会解读数字，所以原来看不太懂的人听完以后也知道大概是什么意思。
父亲自己看不太明白那张单子，只好请医生再解读一遍，免得回家以后还一直想不通。

example_translations.translation: The teacher did not give the standard answer right away. Instead, she first led everyone through those few lines bit by bit, interpreting what they were really trying to say.
The specialist invited onto the news was very good at interpreting numbers, so even the people who had not understood them before knew roughly what they meant after listening.
Father could not really make sense of that form by himself, so he had to ask the doctor to interpret it once more, so that he would not keep thinking about it without understanding after going home.

glosses.notes: To liberate, free something from restraint, or free up time, labor, space, or a person's hands.

examples.sentence: 新机器一进家门，最先让母亲高兴的不是快，而是它真的能解放双手，让她晚上多坐一会儿。
书里写到那个城后来终于被解放的时候，孩子先停了一下，然后马上问后面的人都怎么样了。
把一些小事交给机器以后，父亲总算解放出一点时间，能坐下来认真陪孩子把作业看完。

example_translations.translation: When the new machine first entered the home, what made Mother happiest was not that it was fast, but that it could truly free up her hands and let her sit and rest a little more at night.
When the book described how that city was finally liberated, the child paused for a moment and then immediately asked what happened to the people afterward.
After handing some small tasks over to a machine, Father finally freed up a bit of time and could sit down and carefully go through the child's homework together.

glosses.notes: To explain aloud for other people, or to provide spoken commentary during an event or viewing experience.

examples.sentence: 老师一边走一边解说墙上的旧照片，大家听完以后才知道前面那些人原来是谁。
比赛开始以后，电视里那个人解说得很慢，把每一个动作为什么重要都先讲得特别清楚。
孩子原来只想快快走过去，听完老师的解说以后，反而在最后那个地方站了很久。

example_translations.translation: The teacher explained the old photos on the wall while walking, and only after listening did everyone understand who the people in them had originally been.
After the match began, the person on television commentated very slowly, first explaining very clearly why each movement mattered.
The child had originally only wanted to walk past quickly, but after hearing the teacher's explanation, he instead stood in the last area for a long time.

glosses.notes: To learn from another example, method, or experience and use what is useful without copying it blindly.

examples.sentence: 老师说，别人的办法当然可以借鉴，如果一点不改就拿来用，到自己这里还是会出别的问题。
这家店后来能慢慢好起来，就是因为老板肯低下头去借鉴别人的做法，再想办法改成自己的。
父亲常说，年轻人多看看前人的路不是坏事，借鉴以后还是要自己一步一步走。

example_translations.translation: The teacher says that other people's methods can of course be learned from, but if you use them without changing anything at all, other problems will still appear in your own case.
The reason this shop was able to slowly improve later was that the owner was willing to lower his head, learn from other people's ways of doing things, and then find a way to turn them into his own.
Father often says that it is not a bad thing for young people to look at the paths taken by those before them, but after drawing lessons from them, they still have to walk step by step on their own.

glosses.notes: A ring worn on a finger, often with emotional, family, decorative, or marriage-related meaning.

examples.sentence: 母亲平时很少戴那个戒指，一到家里有重要日子的时候，她还是会先拿出来慢慢擦一遍。
孩子在门口地上看见那个戒指以后，没有乱动，只是赶快回头叫大人出来看看是不是家里掉的。
老人把旧戒指放进小盒子里的时候，顺手又摸了一下，因为那上面还有年轻时留下的印子。

example_translations.translation: Mother rarely wears that ring in daily life, but whenever the family has an important occasion, she still takes it out first and slowly wipes it clean.

After the child saw that ring on the ground by the doorway, he did not touch it carelessly, but quickly turned around and called an adult over to see whether it had been dropped by someone in the family.
When the old man put the old ring into the small box, he touched it once again in passing, because it still had marks left from his younger days.

secondary_glosses: to use with the help of
glosses.notes: To use some tool, force, condition, or outside help as a means to achieve something.

examples.sentence: 第一次走那条山路的人最好借助地图，不然一到分开的地方，就很容易看错方向。
医生借助新的工具看了一会儿以后，很快就指出问题在哪儿，所以大家心里也一下有底了。
老师让我们先借助图片去想那段话到底在说什么，然后再慢慢把里面难懂的地方解开。

example_translations.translation: People walking that mountain road for the first time had better make use of a map, otherwise once they reach the point where the path splits, it becomes easy to take the wrong direction.
After using the new tool for a while, the doctor quickly pointed out where the problem was, so everyone immediately had a clearer sense of things.
The teacher told us to first use the picture to think about what that passage was actually saying, and only then slowly untie the difficult parts inside it.

glosses.notes: The total amount of money involved in a bill, payment, contract, transfer, or other financial matter.

examples.sentence: 父亲拿到单子以后先看的不是东西，而是上面的金额，因为只要那个数不对，后面都得再重来。
她买东西以前总会先问清金额，哪怕差得不多，也不想到了最后才发现自己带的钱不够。
公司后来发现转过去的金额写错了一位，所以两边的人晚上又重新对了一遍，才终于放心回家。

example_translations.translation: After getting the slip, the first thing Father looked at was not the items but the amount on it, because if that number is wrong, everything afterward has to be done again.

Before buying something, she always asks clearly about the amount of money first. Even if the difference is not large, she does not want to discover only at the end that she did not bring enough money.
The company later discovered that one digit in the transferred amount had been written incorrectly, so the people on both sides went through it again that evening before finally going home at ease.
